processed_notes.note_text: David continues to call to check in and let me know he's committed to our program. I let him know that our waitlist is moving slower than usual and could be up to a month or more before he gets a spot. I added him to reentry nav and gave him the info about the SCOUT Motors job fair on Thursday to see if he can find some employment in the meantime.

David called to ask me to call or email his counselor at Transitions shelter so she knows the work he's putting in. If he continues to make progress, he's allowed to stay there, so he wants to show that. I sent an email to Dani confirming he reached out to us, is on our waitlist, and confirmed what our program entails so she knows what he'll be doing once he's accepted. I also included my contact info in case she wants to talk live with me.

Summary: Participant called back to finish his phone consultation. He already knew about the program and didn’t need an overview. He heard about Turn90 from a flyer and from counselors at the prison. He was released from prison on 11/02/2026 and seems a strong fit: stable shelter housing, ID in hand, a GED, mechanic certification, and a long welding background. He was added to the waitlist.

Housing: Staying at a transitional shelter in downtown Columbia (2025 Main St; most likely Transitions). He says he can stay “for a while” as long as he stays productive and keeps making progress. No immediate housing need.

Identification / Documents: Has his SC state ID, Social Security card, GED, and technical college certificates. No birth certificate.

Driver’s License: Not current. He lost the physical card earlier and couldn’t afford a replacement, so he got a state ID instead. Because too much time has passed, he has to retake the license test.

Education / Credentials: Has his GED. Graduated from the Master Automotive & Diesel Technician Training Program at a New York automotive and diesel institute in NYC (exact school name unclear on the recording).

Employment History: Certified automotive/diesel mechanic. Experienced welder (stick, MIG, TIG) who learned on the job but has no welding certification. During this incarceration he spent about 6 months studying the Hobart welding manual and the AWS welding symbols manual. Also has some drywall, landscaping, and cleaning experience. Longest time at one job is 2 years. Past jobs ended because of substance use and incarceration.

Physical Limitations: None reported.

Medications / Health: No current prescriptions. Gets mental health and other support services through the shelter and works with a counselor there.

Substance Use History: Long history of alcohol and drug use, including crack cocaine, cocaine, and heroin (“just about everything”). Reports about 3 years sober, which lines up with his time incarcerated. Past use has led to homelessness. He understands that weekly drug testing includes marijuana and that a failed test means removal from the program.

Criminal Justice History:

First arrest at age 18. Says he has had “too many to count” arrests and has been in and out of the system for most of his adult life.
5 prison terms in SC. Has also been incarcerated in NY, VA, and GA. Couldn’t give a total number of convictions.
Most recent: released from prison 11/02/2026 after about 2.5 years. Charge was burglary 2nd degree (violent), served on a nonviolent basis. No drug trafficking or firearm charge.
No sex offense convictions. No pending charges.
Biological parents: father died when the participant was 10, and his record is unknown. Mother has no criminal record.

Supervision: On parole for about 6 months, with expected completion around April–May 2027. Reports full compliance. Next parole report is 11/12/2026.

Obligations: No dependents. His children are adults (ages 25–30). No child support. The parole report is his only scheduled obligation.

Transportation: Takes the bus. Gets bus passes from his shelter counselor when they’re available. I told him the nearest stop is a 15–20 minute walk from the center, and he said that’s fine.

Availability: Can attend 9am–3pm.

Emergency Needs: None reported.

Program Overview Given: I covered the 8-week program and job placement afterward, the $450 weekly stipend starting after week 2, the point system ($9 lost per point for lateness, phone use in class, or missed homework), and weekly drug testing. He had no questions.

Reentry Navigation: Offered. He declined for now because the shelter’s services and his counselor already cover his needs.

Contact Plan: He has no phone. He will call in to check in and may call daily. I saved the number he called from under his name. If he doesn’t reach me, he’ll leave a voicemail. I told him waitlist updates usually come Mondays or Tuesdays, after Friday orientation. For urgent messages, staff can call the shelter and leave word with his counselor, Danny, who will pass it on. He believes that’s the same number he called from.

Outcome / Next Steps:

Added to the waitlist. Expected wait is 3 weeks or less, but not guaranteed.
Update him on his waitlist position when he checks in on Mondays or Tuesdays.
No phone. He called to schedule the appointment from a Walmart phone. He said he'd give me call when he gets back to the shelter to do the consultation.
